report:
Reviewed the complete selector_test claim, its one ordinary implementation association in review.rs and all five ordinary associated tests. There are no TODO/N/A entries. The selector's three identity fields and fragment path select one annotated function; attributes, signature, body and contained comments are included; Cargo target identity distinguishes identical Rust paths; no enclosing-file snapshot or persisted offsets are required; unrelated preceding lines leave an unchanged selected function fresh.

Implementation: Selector::Test stores only crate_name, target and rust_path. inventory builds function fragments from current correspondence spans and excludes spans/line numbers from ReviewTest and selector metadata. It globally rejects differing spans for the same file/package/target/path, including collisions spread across anchors. select reloads correspondence, rejects diagnostics, filters all three identity components plus canonical source-file equality, deduplicates matching spans and requires exactly one, then returns the exact source slice. input_errors compares freshly resolved fragments, so current byte locations can change without changing the persisted selection. capture_read appends only the selected text. Captured correspondence.rs context confirms Cargo-derived normalized package identity, target kind/name, nested module-qualified paths, annotated eligible test inventory, complete syn function-item spans, and character-aware source offset conversion. This is shared correspondence infrastructure, while selector-specific logic is in the associated review.rs; the additional captured fragments protect the infrastructure used in this assessment.

Test adequacy: test_selector_preserves_metadata_and_ignores_unrelated_line_movement asserts package, lib target, nested qualified path, source file, inherited cfg and ordinary status; capture_read must equal the complete TEST literal, which contains both attributes, signature, full body, internal comment and closing brace. After recording, inserting unrelated lines leaves check valid, whereas changing inherited cfg invalidates it. Fixture setup separates implementation and test source, so the valid movement case also establishes that the enclosing test file need not be snapshotted. test_selectors_disambiguate_identical_paths_by_cargo_target creates two integration targets over the same physical file, asserts two distinct targets, resolves each complete function, and rejects a mismatched package. another_anchors_test_read_tracks_body_and_identity captures a second anchor's function exactly, then verifies body edits, missing identity and duplicate ambiguous identity prevent recording; for nonambiguous edits it proves the primary anchor's initial fragments/metadata are unchanged. ambiguous_initial_test_selector_cannot_be_recorded_as_complete_context rejects duplicate cfg-alternative spans at start or recording and requires a failing gate. ambiguous_test_identity_across_anchors_is_rejected requires start rejection even when colliding paths belong to different anchors. Together these assertions detect partial function extraction, offset-dependent staleness, lost target identity and accidental ambiguous selection. No missing claimed scenario was identified.

Execution is separate: I ran review start and review read commands and inspected current source/assertions; I did not rerun test suites or build. Coordinator reports 331 functional tests plus build/book and latest 31 review tests passing; that execution is not attributed to this reviewer. A historical HEAD output lookup found no prior record, so this assessment relies on current evidence, not inherited approval. No source edits were made. No requested edits.
